meta.name: Sourdough Cinnamon Buns

source.name: Adapted from ATK Ultimate Cinnamon Buns + multi-source sourdough research
source.author: proofed. research synthesis

meta.description: ATK Ultimate Cinnamon Buns rebuilt on a sourdough chassis. Active levain replaces commercial yeast, overnight cold retard develops complex flavor. Same reduced-sugar filling and cream-cheese-forward glaze (v1.2.0). Heavy cream pour before baking for caramel bottom.

change_log.summary: Initial recipe adapted from ATK Ultimate Cinnamon Buns v1.3.0 with sourdough levain, overnight cold retard, springform pan, and heavy cream pour. Based on 7-agent research synthesis (100+ sources).

vessels.name: Levain Jar
vessels.reuse: Build levain → freed after adding to mixer

vessels.name: Stand Mixer Bowl
vessels.reuse: Dough mix → bulk ferment → cold retard → freed after shaping

vessels.name: 23cm Springform Pan
vessels.reuse: Line → arrange rolls → proof → bake → serve

ingredients.name: Ripe Sourdough Starter
ingredients.rationale: 17-20% PFF is consensus for enriched sourdough dough

ingredients.name: Cornstarch
ingredients.rationale: Unchanged from ATK — gluten dilution for tenderness, resistant to sourdough enzymatic degradation

ingredients.name: Unsalted Butter
ingredients.rationale: Unchanged from ATK v1.3.0. 29% baker's % matches Perfect Loaf enrichment level.

ingredients.name: Cream Cheese (softened)
ingredients.rationale: v1.2.0 amount (bumped from 113g for cream-cheese-forward glaze)

ingredients.name: Large Eggs (room temp)
ingredients.rationale: ATK and Perfect Loaf both use 3. Most sourdough recipes use 1. Keeping 3 for ATK DNA.

ingredients.name: Heavy Cream
ingredients.rationale: Poured over rolls before baking. Multiple sourdough recipes endorse 60-120ml range.

states.title: Mix Levain
states.direction: In a clean jar, combine 34g ripe starter, 84g flour, and 84g water. Stir until no dry flour remains. Cover loosely and place at room temperature (~75°F (24°C)).
states.exit_condition: All ingredients combined, no dry flour, covered in jar at room temp

notes.text: Build 6-8 hours before you plan to mix dough. Evening bake: build at 2-4pm. Morning bake: build the night before.
Starter must be active and recently fed — doubled or tripled within 6-8 hours of last feeding.

states.title: Ferment Levain
states.direction: Let levain ferment at room temperature until doubled in volume and bubbly throughout. Should pass the float test.
states.exit_condition: Levain doubled, bubbly, domed top, passes float test (small spoonful floats in water)

notes.text: Timing varies: 6 hrs in warm kitchen (78°F+ (26°C+)), 8+ hrs in cool kitchen (68°F (20°C)). Watch the levain, not the clock.

states.title: Line Springform Pan
states.direction: Place a parchment circle on the base of the 23cm (9-inch) springform pan. Grease sides with butter. Wrap outside bottom in aluminum foil to catch any filling leaks.
states.exit_condition: Parchment on base, sides greased, foil wrapped on exterior bottom

notes.text: Place a sheet pan on the rack below during baking to catch any drips.

states.title: Combine Dough
states.direction: In stand mixer bowl, add 430g flour, 64g cornstarch, 75g sugar, and 9g salt. Whisk briefly by hand to combine. Add 200g ripe levain, 80g warm milk (95-100°F (35-38°C)), and 3 eggs. Attach dough hook. Mix on low until dough is cohesive and wraps around hook, 3-4 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Shaggy dough formed, no dry flour visible, dough wraps around hook

notes.text: Milk should be 95-100°F (35-38°C) — warm enough to help activate levain but not hot enough to kill it. Do not exceed 110°F (43°C).
Optional hybrid: add 1g instant yeast with the dry ingredients for scheduling insurance. Preserves full sourdough flavor at this amount (0.2% baker's %).

states.title: Rest Dough
states.direction: Stop mixer. Cover bowl with plastic wrap or towel. Let dough rest to relax gluten before adding butter.
states.exit_condition: 10 minutes elapsed, dough relaxed

notes.text: This rest makes butter incorporation dramatically easier. Don't skip.

states.title: Incorporate Butter
states.direction: With dough hook on low speed, add 170g softened butter ONE PAT AT A TIME. Wait for each pat to fully incorporate before adding the next. Once all butter is absorbed, increase to medium speed and mix until dough is smooth, glossy, and pulls away from bowl sides.
states.exit_condition: Dough is smooth, glossy, elastic, and cleanly pulls from bowl sides. No visible butter streaks.

notes.text: Butter must be softened, not melted. Finger-press test: leaves indentation but holds shape.
Fat coats gluten strands and prevents cross-linking. Adding butter AFTER gluten development is critical.
If dough is very sticky after all butter is in, continue mixing on medium for 2-3 more minutes. Do not add extra flour.

states.title: Bulk Ferment with Folds
states.direction: Cover dough in bowl. Ferment at room temperature (~75°F (24°C)). At 30 minutes and 60 minutes, perform a set of stretch and folds: pull dough from one side, stretch up and fold over center, rotate 90° and repeat 3 more times. Re-cover after each set.
states.exit_condition: Dough shows 20-30% volume increase. Wobbles when container is shaken (jiggle test). Surface is smooth and slightly domed.

notes.text: Target 20-30% rise, NOT doubled. Enriched dough rises less during bulk than lean dough.
Stretch and fold at 30 min and 60 min. These supplement the mixer kneading — they equalize temperature and redistribute fermentation gases.
If kitchen is cold (<70°F (21°C)), bulk may take 2-3 hours. Watch the dough, not the clock.

states.title: Overnight Cold Retard
states.direction: Cover bowl tightly with plastic wrap. Place in refrigerator at 37-40°F (3-4°C). Retard overnight, minimum 8 hours.
states.exit_condition: Minimum 8 hours in fridge. Dough is cold and firm. Can hold up to 48 hours.

notes.text: Fridge must be below 40°F (4°C). Check with thermometer. Above 40°F risks overproofing.
Most fermentation happens in the first 3-4 hours while dough cools. Flavor develops throughout the retard.
If using hybrid yeast (1g instant), do not retard longer than 24 hours. Commercial yeast is more cold-tolerant than wild cultures.
Cold retard shifts acid balance toward acetic acid (sharper tang). Butter, sugar, and eggs moderate the tanginess — expect subtle complexity, not aggressive sour.

states.title: Make Filling
states.direction: In small bowl, combine 240g brown sugar, 10g cinnamon, and 1.5g salt. Mix until uniform.
states.exit_condition: Filling mixture evenly combined, no clumps

notes.text: Can be made the evening before or morning of. Shelf-stable — cover and set aside.

states.title: Roll Dough into Square
states.direction: Pull cold dough from fridge. Pat into rough square shape with hands on lightly floured surface. Roll from center diagonally toward corners, rotating 90° every few rolls. Target: 46x46cm (18x18 inch) square.
states.exit_condition: Even square with consistent thickness throughout. Run hand over surface to check for hills/valleys.

notes.text: Cold dough from the fridge rolls cleanly — this is a feature of the overnight retard. No sticking, sharp cuts.
If dough resists rolling, let rest 5-10 min at room temp. Cold enriched dough can be stiff.
Use guides (rulers, dowels) alongside dough for even thickness.

states.title: Apply Butter and Filling
states.direction: Spread 57g softened butter evenly over dough, leaving 1cm border at far edge. Sprinkle filling mixture over butter, pressing lightly to adhere.
states.exit_condition: Butter and filling evenly distributed, filling pressed into butter, 1cm bare border at far edge

states.title: Roll Into Cylinder
states.direction: Starting from edge nearest you, roll dough away into tight cylinder, keeping roll taut by tucking as you go. Pinch seam closed. If necessary, gently reshape to even diameter.
states.exit_condition: Tight, even cylinder with sealed seam, ~46cm long

notes.text: Keep tension consistent — loose rolls create gaps in the spiral.

states.title: Cut and Arrange
states.direction: Using bench scraper, cut cylinder in half. Cut each half into 4 equal pieces (8 total). Arrange cut-side up in prepared springform: 7 around the edge, 1 in the center. Cover loosely with plastic wrap.
states.exit_condition: 8 buns arranged cut-side up in springform, covered

notes.text: Rolls should have ~1cm spacing — they expand to touch during final proof.
Try dental floss for cleaner cuts if bench scraper drags the filling.

states.title: Final Proof
states.direction: Let rolls proof at room temperature until doubled, puffy, and touching each other.
states.exit_condition: Rolls doubled, puffy, touching each other. Gentle poke springs back slowly.

notes.text: 1.5-2 hours at 75°F (24°C). Cooler kitchen = longer. Rolls should look pillowy and jiggly.
Start preheating oven 20-30 minutes before proof ends.

states.title: Preheat Oven
states.direction: Heat oven to 375°F (190°C) with rack in middle position.
states.exit_condition: Oven fully preheated to 375°F (190°C)

states.title: Pour Heavy Cream
states.direction: Warm 100g heavy cream slightly (microwave 20 sec or stovetop). Pour evenly over proofed rolls, letting it seep between them.
states.exit_condition: Cream distributed over and between rolls

notes.text: The cream combines with brown sugar filling during baking to create a caramel sauce bottom.
Warm the cream slightly so it settles into the dough rather than pooling on top.

states.title: Bake
states.direction: Place springform on middle rack (sheet pan on rack below to catch drips). Bake until deep golden brown and filling is bubbling.
states.exit_condition: Deep golden brown, filling visibly bubbling. Internal temp 190°F (88°C).

notes.text: Check at 20 min. Springform's higher sides may require 23-25 min total. Rotate pan if browning unevenly.
If top browns too fast, tent loosely with foil for remaining bake time.

states.title: Cool
states.direction: Transfer springform to wire rack. Let cool in pan.
states.exit_condition: Buns warm but not molten-hot. Filling has set slightly.

notes.text: Filling and caramel bottom are extremely hot — wait the full time.
Cooling in the springform lets butter reabsorb into the dough.

states.title: Make Glaze
states.direction: In small bowl (V3, now empty), whisk cream cheese, 15g milk, vanilla, confectioners' sugar, and 0.5g salt until smooth.
states.exit_condition: Smooth, spreadable glaze with no lumps

notes.text: Make during COOL step to save time.

states.title: First Glaze Application
states.direction: Spread HALF the glaze evenly over warm buns while still in springform.
states.exit_condition: First layer of glaze applied, melting slightly into warm buns

states.title: Unmold Buns
states.direction: Unlatch the springform ring and carefully lift it away. Use a large spatula to slide buns (on parchment) to a serving platter or cutting board.
states.exit_condition: Buns transferred to serving surface, springform removed

notes.text: The caramel bottom from the heavy cream should be set enough to hold together. If still liquid, let cool 5 more minutes.

states.title: Final Glaze
states.direction: Spread remaining glaze over top. Serve warm.
states.exit_condition: Buns fully glazed and ready to serve

methods.detail: Room temp, covered. Expected 2-3 day softness (sourdough anti-staling).

techniques.name: Sourdough levain for enriched dough
techniques.sourcedFrom: The Perfect Loaf, King Arthur Baking
techniques.rationale: 17-20% PFF (pre-fermented flour) is the consensus for enriched sourdough. Provides flavor complexity without over-acidifying.

techniques.name: Hybrid leavening (optional commercial yeast)
techniques.sourcedFrom: King Arthur, The Perfect Loaf, Professor Calvel, French pain au levain regulations
techniques.rationale: 0.2% instant yeast provides scheduling insurance while preserving full sourdough character. Flavor-indistinguishable from pure sourdough at this threshold.

techniques.name: Overnight cold retard (bulk)
techniques.sourcedFrom: The Perfect Loaf, Grant Bakes, Heartbeet Kitchen, Little Spoon Farm
techniques.rationale: Cold dough is easier to shape, flavor develops during retard, and the schedule is convenient for morning baking. Bulk retard preferred over shaped retard for enriched dough.

techniques.name: Delayed butter incorporation
techniques.sourcedFrom: The Perfect Loaf, Pastry School 101, The Pantry Mama
techniques.rationale: Fat coats gluten strands and prevents cross-linking. Developing gluten before adding butter is universally recommended for enriched sourdough.

techniques.name: Heavy cream pour before baking
techniques.sourcedFrom: Farmhouse on Boone, Country Roads Sourdough
techniques.rationale: Cream combines with brown sugar filling to create caramel sauce bottom. Keeps rolls ultra-moist during bake.

techniques.name: Springform pan for sourdough cinnamon rolls
techniques.sourcedFrom: The Clever Carrot, Cuisine at Home, Hostess at Heart
techniques.rationale: Higher sides retain moisture during long proof. Easy unmolding preserves spiral tops. 23cm fits 8 rolls in 7+1 arrangement.

research.strategy: 7-agent parallel research: enriched dough science, King Arthur hybrid methodology, cross-reference top recipes, pure vs hybrid debate, tangzhong + sourdough, pan options, overnight scheduling
